title: You’re asking God to grow you…
paragraphs:
You’re asking God to grow you…
but you’re still gripping what He told you to release.
Because this isn’t just about discipline.
It’s about disobedience disguised as delay.

That conviction in the quiet.
That nudge you tried to ignore.
That moment when the Holy Spirit put His finger on that one thing…

Not because God wasn’t clear—
but because obedience would cost you something.

Praying for elevation…
while entertaining what God already exposed.

Crying for breakthrough…
while protecting the very chain that’s choking your calling.
Some of you are holding onto a relationship God already said “release.”

But it feels good.
It fills the loneliness.
It gives you attention your soul craves.

“It’s complicated.”
“It’s not that bad.”
“I’m praying about it.”
Some of you are hiding a secret sin.

Private.
Silent.
But slowly eroding your fire for God.

You still worship.
You still post scriptures.
You still say “God is good.”
And here’s the weight of it:
The Bible doesn’t whisper about this.
“Let us throw off everything that hinders and the sin that so easily entangles…” — Hebrews 12:1

Not manage it.
Not justify it.
Not slowly wean off it.
Because sin doesn’t loosen its grip politely.
And here’s what many don’t realize:

You can’t run your race
while holding onto your chains.

You will either carry your sin…
or carry your calling.
Why is it so hard to let go?
Because that thing you’re holding onto…
But it never tells you the full price.

Because behind the pleasure…
is bondage.
“Then, after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.” — James 1:15
But here’s the turning point—don’t miss this.

God is not exposing your sin
to shame you.

He’s exposing it
to save you.
This is where the Gospel comes in.
Because you and I cannot break our chains by willpower alone.

We promised God “this is the last time”—
and then went back again.
Not just to forgive your sin…
but to destroy its power over you.
“So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.” — John 8:36

Not partially free.
Not temporarily free.
On the cross, Jesus didn’t just carry your guilt.

Your addiction.
Your secret habits.
Your hidden compromises.

He took the punishment you deserved—
so you could receive the freedom you don’t deserve.
But here’s the truth most people avoid:

You cannot hold onto sin
and fully receive grace.
but because your hands are full.
Repentance is not just saying sorry.
It’s releasing what God told you to release.

It’s trusting that what He has for you
is better than what you’re letting go of.
It will feel like loss at first.

That relationship.
That habit.
That version of you.
That thing you’re afraid to release?
That comfort you keep returning to?
What is God asking you to release?
Because on the other side of your obedience…
On the other side of your surrender…
On the other side of your repentance…
is Jesus—waiting, arms open, not condemning, but calling.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9

“Lord Jesus, I confess the things I’ve been holding onto that You told me to release. I repent. I turn away from them. I cannot break these chains on my own—but You can. Set me free, not just in words, but in reality. I surrender everything to You. Amen.”
